verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Every ingredient of the display is present with the paper's exponents, but the triple is never packaged as one Lean object; it travels as separate arguments (velocity, pressure, two stress scalars). Term by term: the sum runs over Finset.range (N+1), i.e. n = 0..N as in the paper; slowOrder h n = 2nh is λ_n (p. 45); finiteProfile N h b f attaches q^(b + λ_n) to the n-th coefficient. The stress scale is angularExponent h = -CoordinateAlgebra.A h - 1/2, so physicalThetaStress and physicalZStress are ∑_{n≤N} q^{-A-1/2+λ_n} T_n, exactly the paper's third entry; prefixStressTheta/prefixStressAxial use the same exponent -A-1/2. For the first two entries the paper's u_n, p_n are the physical coefficients of (5.1), which already carry their q-powers; Lean carries them explicitly — slowFlux with exponent 0 (ru_{r,n} = q^{λ_n}V_n), slowSwirl with -A-1/2 (u_{θ,n} = r q^{-A-1/2+λ_n}φ_n/C), slowAxial with -A (u_{z,n} = q^{-A+λ_n}U_n), slowPressure with -2A (p_n = q^{-2A+λ_n}Π_n). Two formulation differences, both routine: (i) the Lean Cartesian velocity is assembled from the summed profiles by the fixed axisymmetric ansatz (AxisymmetricResidual.velocity, whose components are -x0·B-x1·F, x0·F-x1·B, U) composed with RadialFluxResidual.radialB V = -V/(2s); both maps are linear in the profiles, so assembling the sums equals summing the assembled u_n; (ii) BaseResidual.prefixVelocity is instead defined as the curl of the prefix potential, and is identified with slowVelocity by NavierStokes.BasePrefixIdentity.prefixVelocity_eq_profiles (NavierStokes/BasePrefixIdentity.lean:157), off the axis.
